questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to learn fluent Italian and I have friends in Italy, so when Milan was the only Italian destination it was a no-brainer for me

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: One thing you have to be aware of is the cultural differences between danes and italians. In Denmark everything is usually done in good time, whereas in Italy it is not always the case. So no I wouldn't sat everything was clear, but I found my way around anyway.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, apart from checking in upon arrival at the host university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy, but my friend and I made a facebook post, which a kind lady then commented on and gave me the telephone number of my future proprietor.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It takes a long time to get around Milano on public transport - especially if you live a little out of the city center. I lived in Bovisa and it generally took me 40 min to get to uni at least.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You were very confused when you arrived because it seemed like some of the courses you thought you could take did not exist. Turned out they did, and that I just couldn't figure out how the website worked. They had a couple of different online registration places, which I must admit were quite confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None, apart from messaging the coordinator, who of course was very busy because everyone had issues.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't freak out if the courses don't appear until a couple of days before semester start. They are a little slow on the technological side of things in Milan.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The classes themselves were very accommodating to all levels I would say, but the exams were very uncomfortable and not at all kind to students with anxiety. So the academic level was fine but the way they conducted the exams was humiliating and anxiety provoking as you had to do an oral exam in front of the other students and could be asked about the whole curriculum with no time to prepare.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was often just the professor speaking and the students listening, whereas in Copenhagen we have discussions and group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Anthropology of ai
World Literatures in English
Music and Digital Humanities
British Theatre and Performance Studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the theatre class because it was very different to what I study at home .

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was less expensive than I imagined and clubbing was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some sports

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I partook in a theatre course in a youth prison in Italian, but I don't think you can partake if you don't speak Italian

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Lago di Como - only 50 mins with the train. Also take a couple of days to go to bergamo Cittá Alta.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy for me because I speak Italian and also lived in Firenze in my gap year. But I would not recommend living in Bovisa, because the area did not feel safe to me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No that part was difficult because there was many other danes on exchange and in my classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Administration and structure in class and exams

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the mood of the people and the food and the fashion

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't freak out if things do not go to plan. I forgot to actually register at the uni until three weeks before and I still managed to go.
2. Be prepared for exams that are very different to the danish ones
3. take time to explore the city so that you can find local spots

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I came back fluent in Italian and very grateful to the danish teaching system. It put my own experience at home into perspective. I also enjoyed having other subjects than usual.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My local area. I did not like Bovisa at all. It was ugly and felt unsafe. The 90/91/92 bus that I had to take was horrible. It was difficult to get home after 12 am because the trains and metro stopped going.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
